hypotheses.justification:
The hypothesis `[Finite ι']` is only used by the current proof: `LinearMap.toMatrix_id_eq_basis_toMatrix` (line 173 of the file) needs `[Finite ι']` (and `LinearMap.toMatrix_mulVec_repr` needs `[Finite m]` for its target index), but the identity itself is index-free in `ι'`.

Statements without it:
* `Basis.toMatrix` is defined with no finiteness at all: `def toMatrix (e : Basis ι R M) (v : ι' → M) : Matrix ι ι' R := fun i j ↦ e.repr (v j) i` (line 51), so `b'.toMatrix b : Matrix ι' ι R` needs no hypothesis on `ι'`.
* `Matrix.mulVec` (Data/Matrix/Mul.lean, line 719) only requires `[Fintype n]` for the *summed* index `n = ι`, which is supplied by the section variable `[Fintype ι]`. It returns a plain function `ι' → R`.
* `b'.repr m : ι' →₀ R` coerces to a function `ι' → R` via the unconditional `FunLike` instance on `Finsupp`, so the RHS also elaborates without `[Finite ι']`.

Proof without `[Finite ι']`: fix `i : ι'` and compute. By `Basis.sum_repr` (Defs.lean line 258, `[Fintype ι]`: `∑ j, b.repr m j • b j = m`) and linearity of `b'.repr` (`map_sum`, `map_smul`), `b'.repr m = ∑ j, b.repr m j • b'.repr (b j)`. Evaluating this Finsupp equality at `i` (`Finsupp.coe_finsetSum`, `Finsupp.smul_apply`) gives `b'.repr m i = ∑ j, b.repr m j * b'.repr (b j) i`. On the other hand `(b'.toMatrix b *ᵥ b.repr m) i = ∑ j, b'.toMatrix b i j * b.repr m j = ∑ j, b'.repr (b j) i * b.repr m j` by `Matrix.mulVec_apply_eq_sum`, `Basis.toMatrix_apply` (line 55, definitional: `e.toMatrix v i j = e.repr (v j) i`), and `mul_comm`. Hence the two functions agree by `funext`; only the finite sum over `ι` is used, and `ι'` never needs to be finite.

Degenerate cases check out: if `ι = ∅` then `M` is trivial, so `m = 0`, `b.repr m = 0`, and both sides are the zero function; if `m = 0` both sides are `0`; if `R` is the trivial (subsingleton) semiring, all entries of the sum and of `b'.repr m` are `0`, so both sides are the zero function. (Independently, when `R` is nontrivial the conclusion is even derivable, since `M` is finite because it has the finite basis `b` and the basis vectors of `b'` are distinct.)

The remaining arguments cannot be deleted: `[Fintype ι]` is required to elaborate `*ᵥ` (the sum over `ι`), `R`, `M`, `[CommSemiring R]`, `[AddCommMonoid M]`, `[Module R M]`, `ι`, `ι'`, `b`, `b'`, `m` all occur in the statement (`b` also occurs in the type of `b.repr m : ι →₀ R`).
